$comment: Frozen conformance vectors for the EarnProof webhook signing scheme. Generated once and committed deliberately: a mismatch means the wire protocol changed, which is a breaking change for every integrator. Do not regenerate to make a test pass. Every secret here is synthetic and grants nothing.

positive.description: Typical proof.created envelope as emitted by the API.
proof.revoked envelope; a second event type over the same secret.
Multi-byte UTF-8 in the body. Fails any implementation that hashes UTF-16 code units or Latin-1 bytes.
Body full of literal dots. Fails any implementation that reconstructs the signing base by splitting on '.' instead of joining.
Zero-length body. The signing base is still timestamp + '.' + deliveryId + '.'.
Body ends with a newline. Fails any receiver that trims the body before verifying.
Indented JSON with newlines. Fails any receiver that re-serialises the parsed object before verifying.
Secret containing multi-byte UTF-8. The HMAC key is the raw UTF-8 bytes of the secret.
64-character hex secret, matching the shape the API issues. The key is the ASCII text of the hex string, NOT the decoded bytes.
Timestamp beyond the signed 32-bit epoch limit. Fails implementations using a 32-bit time type.
8 KiB body, to exercise streaming body collection.

negative.description: One character of the payload changed after signing.
A single trailing space added after signing. Byte-for-byte comparison is the whole point.
Semantically identical JSON with reordered keys. Verifying a re-serialised object instead of the raw bytes would wrongly accept this.
Signature produced with a different secret.
Correctly signed but older than the tolerance window: a captured delivery being replayed later.
Correctly signed but dated beyond the tolerance window in the future.
Valid signature over one timestamp, a different timestamp in the header. The header must be the value that was signed.
Valid signature over one delivery ID, a different one in the header.
Bare hex digest with no 'v1=' prefix.
Unknown scheme version. A receiver must reject rather than guess.
Correct digest in uppercase. The canonical encoding is lowercase hex; accepting both widens the comparison surface for no benefit.
Digest truncated to 32 hex characters. A prefix comparison would wrongly accept this.
Correct length, non-hexadecimal characters.
Empty signature header value.
Signature header not sent at all.
Timestamp header not sent at all.
Delivery header not sent at all.
Non-numeric timestamp header.
Fractional seconds. The scheme signs whole seconds; '1724400000.5' would also change how the base string splits.
Milliseconds instead of seconds — a common porting bug. Lands far outside the tolerance window.

replayScenarios.description: The same delivery ID arrives twice. The second must be recognised as already processed and must not run side effects again.
A retry of a delivery the receiver never finished processing. Because nothing was recorded, the retry is accepted normally.
An unauthenticated request carrying a valid delivery ID but a bad signature must NOT reserve that delivery ID. Recording before verifying lets anyone suppress a genuine delivery.
A delivery captured off the wire and replayed after the tolerance window. Rejected on the timestamp before the signature is even considered valid grounds to act.

rotationScenarios.description: During a rotation window the receiver holds both secrets. A delivery signed with either one verifies.
Once the old secret is dropped, deliveries signed with it no longer verify.
